Team — forwarding NimbusPay escalation. High-level observations from initial metrics:
- Reserved pool for NimbusPay (us-west-2) shows sustained GPU utilization at 98-99% since 15:45 UTC.
- Cross-region routing traces show a spike in requests from eu-west-1 routed to us-west-2 due to a routing config change this morning.
- Background model warming/quantization batches are running across the same pool (long jobs queued).

Immediate asks:
1) Can we enable emergency fallback routing to NimbusPay's secondary pool in us-east-1?
2) Throttle non-critical background workloads and pause scheduled batch jobs on that pool.
3) Temporarily bump burst capacity for NimbusPay's reservation (if policy allows).

Marcus / Naomi — can you own 1 & 2? Vivek / Tessa — I'll keep Jared updated.

Jonas

On it. Quick findings from ops:
- Root cause: a routing policy change deployed at 08:12 local (automated rollout) accidentally widened the regional affinity rule. That caused eu-west-1 traffic to prefer the us-west-2 pool for certain model variants. Combined with an unrelated long-running quantization job that started at 14:40, the pool hit headroom exhaustion.

Mitigations we will apply now (target: within 20 minutes):
- Push emergency routing rollback (revert affinity rule) to restore correct regional splits. (Marcus — executing now.)
- Pause long-running quantization/warmup jobs on the affected pool. (Naomi — pausing jobs now.)
- Apply temporary burst allowance to NimbusPay's reservation for the next 60 minutes to drain queue. (Vivek — approving the manual increase.)

I'm attaching a tiny patch to the ops runbook that codifies the rollback steps.

Attachments: [Attachment: ops_runbook_patch.txt (ops runbook diff)]

I'll post back once all three are confirmed.

Marcus Lin
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
